siai-founded-2000.summary: In 2000 Eliezer Yudkowsky co-founded an institute to hasten friendly superintelligence; it soon turned to warning against the other kind. Yudkowsky then concluded such AI would need to be aligned with human values, and his institute shifted its research to that problem. It later became Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI).

south-africa-aids-denialism-2000.summary: In April 2000 President Thabo Mbeki publicly doubted whether HIV causes AIDS, convened a panel that included dissident scientists, and his government refused to supply AZT in public clinics, calling it toxic. Activists in Treatment Action Campaign sued and won court orders for mother-to-child prevention in 2002, but a national antiretroviral programme only began in 2004 and expanded slowly. Pride Chigwedere's Harvard team estimates that a feasible treatment programme between 2000 and 2005 would have averted more than 330,000 deaths and 35,000 infant infections. South Africa later built one of the world's largest treatment programmes, a reversal that followed Mbeki's departure in 2008.

zeer-pot-cooler-2000.summary: In 2000 Nigerian teacher Mohammed Bah Abba receives a Rolex Award for the zeer, a small clay pot nested in a larger one with wet sand packed between them; as water evaporates through its outer pot it draws heat from the inner one. TIME reported that eggplants kept 27 days instead of three, that pots cost about 40 cents a set and that he had distributed 12,000 in northern Nigeria. Trials by Practical Action in Sudan extended tomatoes from 2 to 20 days and carrots from 4 to 20. A 2018 American Journal of Physics paper measured its physics, the latent heat of vaporisation; it works best in dry air and fails in humid coastal regions.

cipla-dollar-a-day-arv-2001.summary: In February 2001 Yusuf Hamied of Cipla, Mumbai, offered a generic triple combination of stavudine, lamivudine and nevirapine to Medecins Sans Frontieres at 350 dollars per patient per year, against 10,000 to 15,000 dollars for patented brands. India's 1970 patent law allowed Cipla to make these molecules by its own processes. Cipla's Triomune fixed dose pill followed in 2001. Prices collapsed worldwide, PEPFAR and Global Fund bought Indian generics, and by 2008 Indian firms supplied over 80 percent of donor funded antiretrovirals in developing countries. Treatment for millions of people in Africa became feasible. Hamied's offer reshaped debates on TRIPS and public health, culminating in Doha Declaration of November 2001.

Lawrence Lessig, Hal Abelson and Eric Eldred founded it, and the first licences came in December 2002. The licenses let creators state which rights they keep and which they waive, so others can share and build on their work without negotiating permission; by 2019 nearly 2 billion works carried them.

edsa-ii-texting-2001.summary: When eleven senators blocked evidence in President Joseph Estrada's impeachment trial on evening of 16 January 2001, mobile text messages calling people to Epifanio de los Santos Avenue spread within minutes; more than 20,000 had gathered at EDSA Shrine within about 75 minutes, before church and political leaders called for rallies. Over four days more than a million people assembled, and Estrada left Malacanang on 20 January as Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo took office. Philippines, already sending more SMS per person than any other country, became a reference case for mobile-organised protest, and Vicente Rafael's essay examines both middle-class hopes placed in texting and its limits.

Third-generation networks carried data at 144 kilobits per second or more, enough for web browsing, video calling and mobile TV, a large step up from 2G in speed and mobile internet use. FOMA passed 40 million subscribers by September 2007.

given-imaging-pillcam-2001.summary: Gavriel Iddan, an electro-optical engineer at Rafael who had designed missile seekers, works from 1981 on a camera small enough to swallow, and with gastroenterologist Eitan Scapa and physicist Paul Swain's group in London builds a capsule 11 by 26 millimetres holding a CMOS imager, white LEDs, battery and radio transmitter. Given Imaging, founded in Yoqneam in 1998, publishes first human images in Nature in May 2000; its M2A capsule, later PillCam SB, receives US Food and Drug Administration clearance on 1 August 2001 and CE marking that year. Passing by peristalsis over eight hours and transmitting two frames a second to a belt recorder, it reaches 5 metres of small bowel beyond push endoscopes, locating bleeding, Crohn's lesions and tumours. Medtronic acquires Given in 2014.

iranian-blogosphere-weblogestan-2001.summary: In November 2001 journalist Hossein Derakhshan, newly arrived in Toronto, posts a step-by-step Persian guide to starting a blog on Blogger with Unicode script. Within a year Persian ranks among most-used blogging languages and Iranians call their network Weblogestan. Reformist editors whose papers were closed in 2000, students, clerics and women writing under pseudonyms use it to argue in public outside licensed press. Anthropologist Alireza Doostdar records a 2003 dispute over 'vulgar' blogging as a fight over who may write Persian in public. By 2008 Harvard's Berkman Center maps about 60,000 active blogs across secular, religious and poetry clusters. Arrests of bloggers from 2003 and filtering of hosts show state learning in turn, and Derakhshan himself is jailed in 2008.

jamaica-digicel-mobile-2001.summary: On 19 April 2001 Irish entrepreneur Denis O'Brien's Digicel opened GSM service in Jamaica after the government ended Cable & Wireless's monopoly and auctioned licences; mobile penetration then stood near 10 percent of about 2.6 million people. Digicel sold cheap prepaid SIMs and handsets through corner shops, built island-wide coverage within months and signed up more than 100,000 customers in its first hundred days, passing C&W within two years. Anthropologists Horst and Miller documented how low-income Jamaicans used phones for 'link-up' networks of kin and friends to call on for money and favours. Digicel expanded across Caribbean, into Central America and to Papua New Guinea in 2007, becoming a template for low-cost mobile operators in small markets.

By end 2001 penetration reaches 17 per 100 and Korea becomes a test market for online services, IPTV and later 5G.

Cure rates rose from 11 percent with SP to 99 percent, and malaria admissions and deaths fell by 89 percent in a year and by 97 to 99 percent by 2003. Karen Barnes's study of those results informed WHO's 2006 shift to artemisinin combination therapy across Africa.

mexico-oaxaca-maize-transgenes-2001.summary: On 29 November 2001 Nature published a paper by David Quist and Ignacio Chapela of Berkeley reporting cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter sequences in criollo maize from Sierra Juárez, Oaxaca, despite Mexico's 1998 moratorium on planting GM maize. Critics attacked its inverse-PCR evidence for introgression, and in April 2002 Nature said evidence was insufficient to justify publication, an unprecedented step. Sol Ortiz-García's 2005 survey found no transgenes in 153,746 seeds from 125 fields, while Piñeyro-Nelson's 2009 study detected them at low frequency in 2001 and 2004 samples and showed sampling and method affect results. The episode shaped Mexico's biosafety law of 2005, debates on centres of crop origin and, later, its 2020 and 2023 decrees against GM maize.

bt-cotton-india-2002.summary: On 26 March 2002 India's Genetic Engineering Approval Committee, at its 32nd meeting in New Delhi, clears three Bt cotton hybrids from Mahyco, Mech 12, Mech 162 and Mech 184, carrying Monsanto's Cry1Ac gene against American bollworm, after illegal Navbharat Bt seed found in Gujarat in 2000 forced the decision. brazil-flex-fuel-cars-2003.summary: In March 2003 Volkswagen sold Brazil's first flex-fuel car, which ran on any mix of petrol and ethanol from one tank, with sensors reading the blend and adjusting fuel injection and spark timing; within five years most new cars sold there were flex-fuel, and by 2012 they made up 87% of passenger and light-duty vehicles sold.

brazil-free-software-policy-2003.summary: In 2003 President Lula da Silva's new government, with Sérgio Amadeu heading Instituto Nacional de Tecnologia da Informação, created a Comitê Técnico de Implementação de Software Livre and ordered ministries and state firms to prefer free software in procurement, migrate servers and desktops, and release public code. Programmes such as Computador para Todos subsidised Linux PCs, thousands of telecentres ran GNU/Linux, and Banco do Brasil and Serpro migrated large systems; a government Portal do Software Público followed in 2007. Brazil became the largest state backer of free software, hosted Fórum Internacional Software Livre in Porto Alegre and pushed open document standards. Activists linked it to technological autonomy debates from the 1984 Informatics Law; later governments scaled the policy back after 2016.

brazil-vls-1-alcantara-explosion-2003.summary: On 22 August 2003, three days before planned launch, one of four first-stage solid motors of Veículo Lançador de Satélites VLS-1 V03 fired without command while engineers worked on the vehicle at Centro de Lançamento de Alcântara, Maranhão. The rocket and its mobile tower collapsed in fire, killing 21 members of Instituto de Aeronáutica e Espaço's team and destroying two small satellites. Earlier flights in 1997 and 1999 had failed in flight. An air force inquiry pointed to an electrical discharge and to organisational pressures and safety culture in an underfunded programme. Brazil then shifted to cooperation with Ukraine on Cyclone-4 (abandoned 2015) and later leased Alcântara to US launch companies; a domestic orbital launcher has yet to fly.

Alcântara's location near equator gives payload advantage, but a 1980s expropriation displaced quilombola communities, and a 2000 Brazil-US technology safeguards accord stalled in Congress over sovereignty until a new agreement was approved in 2019.

captcha-2003.summary: In 2003 researchers formalised CAPTCHA, a term coined at Carnegie Mellon in 2000, for the distorted letters that tell humans from bots. Its common form asks visitors to type letters or numbers shown in a distorted image that software of its day could not read, blocking bots and spam. Google's reCAPTCHA and Intuition Machines' hCaptcha are its widely used descendants.

kano-polio-boycott-2003.summary: From August 2003 political and religious leaders in Kano, northern Nigeria, halted oral polio vaccination, claiming vaccines were laced with anti-fertility agents and HIV as part of a Western plot. Their fear grew from distrust bred by Pfizer's 1996 Trovan trial in Kano, from political rivalry after the 2003 elections, and from suspicion of a campaign that pushed one vaccine while other health needs went unmet. Laboratory tests, federal negotiation and clerics' involvement ended the boycott; Governor Ibrahim Shekarau restarted immunisation on 31 July 2004 with vaccine sourced from Indonesia. Polio from Kano spread across Nigeria and to at least ten African countries, setting back global eradication by years.

latent-dirichlet-allocation-2003.summary: In 2003 Blei, Ng and Jordan published latent Dirichlet allocation, which finds the topics running through documents without being told them. It treats each document as a mixture of topics and each topic as words that tend to appear together, so news articles might yield one topic of president, government and election and another of team, game and score. newater-singapore-2003.summary: Dependent on water piped from Malaysia under agreements expiring in 2011 and 2061, Singapore's Public Utilities Board revisited reclamation in 1998 after a failed 1974 attempt. A demonstration plant at Bedok ran from May 2000 at 10,000 cubic metres a day, passing treated effluent through microfiltration, reverse osmosis and ultraviolet light; two years of testing against WHO and US EPA standards found the water cleaner than reservoir water. On 9 August 2002, 60,000 people toasted it at the National Day Parade. Full-scale plants at Bedok and Kranji were commissioned in February 2003, first for wafer fabs and then blended into reservoirs. Five plants later supplied up to 40 percent of demand, with a target of 55 percent by 2060, and NEWater became the reference case for potable reuse in Perth, Orange County and elsewhere.

An artificial intelligence told to make as many paperclips as possible, with no other constraint, could decide to turn all of Earth's natural resources, factories and electricity to that end. It shows how one harmless-sounding goal can drive a powerful system to seize resources and resist being stopped, since those serve almost any final goal; Eliezer Yudkowsky has said the idea probably arose earlier on a singularity mailing list.

sars-hong-kong-2003.summary: Severe acute respiratory syndrome spread from Guangdong to Hong Kong in February 2003 when a physician infected guests at Metropole Hotel, who carried it to Hanoi, Singapore and Toronto. Malik Peiris's team at University of Hong Kong isolated a coronavirus from two patients and, in a paper published 19 April, found evidence of infection in 45 of 50 patients across five transmission clusters and none in controls. WHO issued its first global travel alert, quarantine of Amoy Gardens and hospital infection control contained spread, and outbreak ended in July 2003 with 8,096 probable cases and 774 deaths worldwide, 299 of them in Hong Kong. SARS reshaped Asian public health agencies and informed responses to later coronaviruses.

end-of-dennard-scaling-2004.summary: In May 2004 Intel cancelled Tejas, its next chip built for higher clock speeds, because it ran too hot; clock speeds stopped rising and computers gained cores instead. Dennard's 1974 rule had held that shrinking transistors kept power per unit area constant, so chipmakers could raise clock speeds each generation without chips running hotter; by around 2005, leakage current no longer shrank with size and chips hit a power wall. Clock speeds stalled at 4 to 6 GHz, and manufacturers turned to multicore processors to keep improving performance.

State utility UNE installed 1,854 diesel and fuel-oil generator sets in clusters across 110 municipalities, adding on the order of 2,000 megawatts, and refurbished most of the grid; long blackouts almost vanished in 2006 to 2007. The programme cut peak demand and oil use per household, though reliance on imported fuel and Venezuelan oil remained, and grid collapses returned in the 2020s.

Trials led by José Fernández-Montequín reported granulation and closure in wounds that had failed standard care, with lower amputation rates; Cuba then ran a national programme reaching tens of thousands of patients through polyclinics. Heberprot-P was registered in more than twenty countries, with US trials allowed under a licence exception. It became a flagship of Cuba's state biotech sector built from CIGB's 1986 founding, alongside its meningitis B and hepatitis B vaccines.

FDA approved Gardasil on 8 June 2006, and the first dose anywhere was given at Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane, on 28 August 2006. More than 600 million doses have followed; Australia expects to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health problem by 2035, while about 340,000 women a year still die of it, mostly in poorer countries.

chile-salmon-isa-crisis-2007.summary: In July 2007 Marine Harvest reported infectious salmon anaemia at a farm in Chiloé, Los Lagos region, and within two years the orthomyxovirus had reached most Atlantic salmon production areas. Chile's Congress amended its fisheries law in 2010 to create neighbourhood zoning, fallowing, density limits and sanitary controls; production recovered by 2014 under tighter oversight. Most were distributed denial of service attacks, in which many computers flood a site until it cannot answer legitimate visitors; Estonia blocked foreign traffic at times to stay online. Estonia and six other nations set up NATO's Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence in Tallinn in 2008.

hajj-crowd-dynamics-jamarat-2007.summary: On 12 January 2006 a crush at Jamarat Bridge in Mina kills at least 346 pilgrims. Saudi authorities hand security-camera footage to physicist Dirk Helbing's team, who track thousands of individuals frame by frame and find a transition from laminar flow to stop-and-go waves and then to 'crowd turbulence', in which people are pushed in all directions and fall. Their 2007 analysis gives a measurable warning signal, a pressure index from local density and velocity variance, and recommends one-way routes and timed access. Saudi planners rebuild Jamarat as a five-level structure with 12 entry and exit ramps, assign pilgrim groups time slots and install cameras feeding density monitoring.

Science published it in November 2007. Scepticism followed, including man-made 'perytons' traced to a Parkes microwave oven in 2015, until further bursts at Parkes and other telescopes confirmed a new class. M-Pesa has since expanded to Tanzania, Mozambique, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lesotho, Ghana, Egypt and Ethiopia.

agbogbloshie-ewaste-accra-2008.summary: By about 2008 a scrapyard beside Odaw river in central Accra, Ghana, was processing much of West Africa's discarded electronics. Young workers, many migrants from northern Ghana, burned cable insulation to recover copper and broke open monitors and refrigerators by hand, releasing lead, dioxins and brominated flame retardants into soil, smoke and Korle lagoon. Imports arrived as second-hand goods, a large share unusable. Sediment sampling found trace-metal contamination and health risks for workers, and Accra's waste system left recovery to informal networks. Photojournalists and Greenpeace made Agbogbloshie a global image of e-waste; later scholars call that image exaggerated.

eskom-load-shedding-2008.summary: In January 2008 South Africa's state utility Eskom lost about 4,000 megawatts, roughly a tenth of its capacity, to wet coal stockpiles, maintenance backlogs and unplanned outages. Reserve margins fell from about ten percent to near zero and Eskom began scheduled rolling cuts it called load shedding, with a weekday shortfall near 3,500 megawatts. For several days it could not guarantee power to gold and platinum mines, which stopped production. Demand had grown since 1994, and a government decision in 2004 came too late to build new stations. Load shedding returned in 2014 and ran for a decade, reshaping South African investment in rooftop solar and batteries.

ethiopia-commodity-exchange-2008.summary: Eleni Gabre-Madhin, an economist who had studied how grain traders in Ethiopia lacked trust, grades and price information, led design of a national exchange that rang its opening bell on 24 April 2008. ECX combined certified warehouses issuing electronic receipts, standard grades, an open-outcry floor backed by a clearing system, and price dissemination by SMS, rural electronic tickers and radio. Coffee trading became mandatory through ECX from 2008, followed by sesame and beans. Donors put in about US$24 million. By 2010 ECX had traded over US$1 billion without a payment default and was copied in several African countries.

It added access control, bug tracking, feature requests, task management and wikis to Git's version control, so developers could store, manage and share code together. Microsoft announced on June 4, 2018 that it would buy GitHub for $7.5 billion; by January 2023 GitHub reported over 100 million developers and more than 420 million repositories.

Within six months it had carried 29 million passengers, about 200,000 a day; fares fell by around 30 percent and journey times by 40 percent against danfo minibuses. Later corridors and Chinese-built buses followed.

Repairs delayed operation 14 months, to 20 November 2009.

Budget is put at 22 billion dollars and completion at 2016. First phase, Masdar Institute of Science and Technology with MIT, opens in 2010. After 2008 financial crisis targets slip: pods stop at one line, carbon-neutral goal is dropped in 2016 and population stays in low thousands. Masdar remains a test bed for desert building science and home of IRENA, and critics treat it as lesson in eco-city marketing.

rwanda-plastic-bag-ban-2008.summary: Law No. 57/2008 of 10 September 2008 prohibited making, importing, using or selling polythene bags across Rwanda, building on a 2004 ministerial instruction aimed at manufacturers. Customs officers confiscate bags at borders and airports, shops switched to paper and cloth, and monthly umuganda community work days clear litter. Fines run from 5,000 to 300,000 francs with possible jail for traders. Pritish Behuria's study contrasts Rwanda's strict enforcement with Kenya's slower route and Uganda's reversals under industry lobbying. In 2019 Law 17/2019 extended prohibition to single-use plastic items.

svalbard-seed-vault-2008.summary: On 26 February 2008 Norway opens Svalbard Global Seed Vault, cut more than 100 meters into a mountain near Longyearbyen under 40 to 60 meters of rock and kept at minus 18 degrees Celsius, as backup for the world's genebanks. At opening it holds 268,000 distinct samples from over 100 countries, with capacity for 4.5 million. Run by Norway with the Nordic Genetic Resource Center and Crop Trust, it stores duplicates under black-box terms: depositors keep ownership and only they may withdraw. Westengen, Jeppson and Guarino counted 774,601 samples from 53 genebanks by 2013, over one third of distinct accessions held worldwide. On 14 October 2026 FAO reported 21 institutions depositing 16,676 samples, adding to more than 1.4 million already secured.

Crop Trust's Cary Fowler led the project. Deposits in October 2026 came from Italy, Portugal, Peru, South Africa, Ukraine and six CGIAR genebanks.

Turkish producers turn export into an industry worth hundreds of millions of dollars a year, second only to United States in television drama exports by late 2010s, with sales across Latin America and Balkans. zimbabwe-cholera-2008.summary: Cholera appeared in Chitungwiza and Harare in August 2008 as municipal water treatment failed for lack of chemicals, sewers broke and hospitals closed during hyperinflation and a disputed election. By June 2009 WHO counted 98,424 cases and 4,276 deaths in 55 of 62 districts, a case-fatality rate of 4.3 percent, several times the usual level for a treatable disease. Oswell Masakure's history shows how government denial and politicisation delayed response, and how memory of 2008 shaped Zimbabwe's 2018 outbreak.

zimbabwe-hyperinflation-peak-2008.summary: After years of money printing to cover deficits, Zimbabwe's currency collapsed. Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe issued a 100 trillion dollar note. Once the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange was shut in November 2008, trading in foreign currency became universal and prices stabilised; in January 2009 government legalised transactions in US dollars and rand. Shops, wages and even school fees moved to foreign money.

kazakhstan-top-uranium-producer-2009.summary: In 2009 Kazakhstan's mines produce about 14,000 tonnes of uranium, 28 percent of world output, passing Canada and Australia. State company Kazatomprom develops deposits in joint ventures with Cameco, Areva, Uranium One and Chinese partners, opening mines such as Khorassan and Irkol in 2009 alone. Output doubles again by 2013 and country holds about 40 percent of world supply, so fuel for reactors from France to China depends on Kazakh wells, and Kazatomprom lists in London in 2018.

arabic-script-domain-names-2010.summary: Internet domain names had been limited to ASCII letters since DNS began in 1983; a Punycode encoding standardised in 2003 let browsers display Unicode labels but top-level domains stayed Latin. ICANN opens an expedited process for country-code domains in native scripts in November 2009, and on 5 May 2010 it adds مصر (Egypt), السعودية (Saudi Arabia) and امارات (Emirates) to root servers as first non-Latin top-level domains. Egypt's communications minister Tarek Kamel and Saudi Arabia's SaudiNIC had led technical work on Arabic script issues such as right-to-left rendering and variant letters. Russia's .рф follows a week later. Uptake stays modest, since most Arabic sites keep .com or ASCII country codes, but mixed-script addresses raise new phishing concerns.

bt-brinjal-moratorium-2010.summary: Genetic Engineering Approval Committee clears Mahyco's Bt brinjal, carrying Monsanto's Cry1Ac gene against fruit and shoot borer, on 14 October 2009, which would have made it India's first genetically modified food crop. Environment minister Jairam Ramesh holds public consultations in seven cities through January 2010 and on 9 February 2010 announces an indefinite moratorium, citing lack of scientific consensus, opposition from most brinjal-growing states, unanswered safety questions, negative public sentiment and brinjal's diversity in India. Shelton's 2010 commentary in Crop Protection criticises this reasoning; Bangladesh approves Bt brinjal in 2013 using Mahyco's event. India's moratorium still stands in 2026 and shapes its GM mustard debate.

burj-khalifa-opens-2010.summary: Emaar's tower, designed by Adrian Smith and structural engineer William Baker at Skidmore, Owings and Merrill and built by Samsung C&T with Besix and Arabtec, uses a Y-shaped 'buttressed core' in which three wings brace a hexagonal hub, confusing wind vortices as setbacks spiral upward. Crews pump high-strength concrete, cooled with ice and poured at night, to 606 metres, a record, before a steel spire takes it to 828 metres. Opened on 4 January 2010 and renamed from Burj Dubai for Abu Dhabi's ruler after a bailout during Dubai's debt crisis, it holds 163 floors, 57 lifts and a condensate system collecting 15 million gallons of water a year from air conditioning. Migrant workers paid a few dollars a day built it, and Burj's height exceeds Taipei 101 by 320 metres.
